heading: Melbourne
description: A map of the City of Melbourne inside Greater Melbourne, with toggleable layers: the city centre and the inner north and south, its suburbs, known-as names, landmarks, trains, trams, V/Line, freeways and main streets, and a suburb lens from the 2021 Census.

living.caveat: 2021 Census figures, not current prices; rents and repayments are averages of small-area medians. Rent is what renting households paid, counting long-time tenants and public housing, so it sits below what a new lease costs. Use them to compare suburbs, not to budget.
living.footer: 2021 Census (Australian Bureau of Statistics), {name}. Counted in August 2021, in lockdown with the border shut, so the City's student population was low. Tiers compare the City of Melbourne's suburbs.

steps.title: North and south of the river
steps.text: Melburnians place a suburb by which side of the Yarra it's on: north of the river or south of it. The City of Melbourne is the city centre and the inner suburbs around it. Greater Melbourne's other 30 councils run the rest.

steps.title: Suburbs, not neighbourhoods
steps.text: Australians give their suburb, not a neighbourhood: Carlton, Southbank, North Melbourne. The names in italics are places people say that aren't suburbs of their own, like Chinatown, the Paris End and Lygon Street.

steps.title: Trains and trams
steps.text: Metro trains fan out from Flinders Street through the City Loop and, since November 2025, the Metro Tunnel. Melbourne kept its trams when other cities tore theirs up, and runs the largest tram network in the world.

steps.title: Tap anywhere
steps.text: Tap any spot or search an address, and the card shows the suburb it's in and what living there is like. Switch layers on and off in the panel to explore.
